sourceRefs.locator: The exhibition at Aðalstræti 16, in the original location of the tenth-century hall. The listing distinguishes the earlier wall fragment. Map point at 64.14749° N, 21.94251° W locates the exhibition on the archaeological site.

FS243-00162, Summary, the paved structure at the eastern doorway. Appendix 4, Karen B. Milek, sections on preservation of occupation deposits and the central hearth. Floor deposits were sealed by collapsed turf roofing.

NORSEC 2, pp. 1–4 and Figs. 5–7. Square-metre sampling, sieving heavy fraction through 1 mm mesh, about 3% identifiable, taxa and calcination. Authors interpret spatial distributions as possible hearth raking and trampling near walls and benches.
Aðalstræti 16; location on the map embedded in the city visitor entry.
